title: Modular evolvability in rapid Japanese Cirsium radiation
core_question: Why did one young Japanese radiation generate large capitulum and ecological disparity so quickly?
prediction: Pre-existing genetic/developmental variation can be reused/recombined so phenotype diverges faster than genome-wide lineage sorting.
primary_systems: Japanese dominant radiation; Ryukyu focal system
required_data: Population ancestry + phenotype + plastid + cytotype + functional/mechanistic follow-up
success_criterion: Aim 1-3 jointly discriminate historical source, adaptive value and mechanistic reuse.

title: Historical/genomic source of rapid phenotypic divergence
core_question: Are repeated capitulum states produced by standing variation and/or introgression, modified by cytotype and cytonuclear history?
prediction: Repeated states need not follow species-level ancestry; local ancestry and plastid/cytotype patterns should distinguish standing variation, introgression and lineage-specific mutation.
primary_systems: C. brevicaule; C. irumtiense; C. pendulum; C. sieboldii; takaoense anchor; lineare/dipsacolepis controls
required_data: Same-individual standardized phenotype + nuclear population ancestry + plastid haplotype + flow cytometry
success_criterion: At least two independent systems discriminate variant-origin alternatives.

title: Adaptive function of capitulum modules
core_question: Which rapidly divergent capitulum modules reduce or redistribute the established antagonist fitness cost, and what pollination or abiotic costs accompany that protection?
prediction: Orientation, colour and validated involucre/spine changes should alter mutualist/antagonist or abiotic pathways and final seed output; defence benefits may trade off against pollinator access.
primary_systems: Ryukyu focal populations first; replicated mainland transition where feasible
required_data: Quantitative antagonist baseline meta-analysis + ancestry-linked trait manipulation + effective pollination/abiotic/antagonist measurements + total and filled seed output
success_criterion: Orientation first; then colour; demonstrate a replicated trait -> interaction/protection -> reproductive-fitness link for at least one module while retaining mutualist and antagonist outcomes separately.

title: Flower-colour reversibility as a mechanistic case of modular reuse
core_question: Are repeated white-coloured transitions enabled by retention and regulatory reuse of anthocyanin machinery?
prediction: Independent W/C transitions should often retain pathway genes while differing in regulatory/expression/pigment state rather than requiring repeated pathway destruction/rebuilding.
primary_systems: C. brevicaule/C. irumtiense; takaoense; pendulum or sieboldii replicate
required_data: Same-individual ancestry + coding/regulatory haplotype + floral RNA + pigment + standardized colour
success_criterion: At least two independent W/C transitions resolve whether regulatory reuse is recurrent.

title: Rapid-radiation premise
core_question: Is there enough radiation asymmetry to justify the system?
prediction: One dominant young Japanese radiation contains 36/38 sampled concepts with rare secondary histories.
success_criterion: No new sampling required for descriptive premise.

title: Secondary-history controls
core_question: Does the dominant radiation differ from secondary Japanese histories?
prediction: lineare/dipsacolepis provide comparison without becoming standalone thesis chapters.
required_data: Minimum population ancestry + phenotype when resources permit
success_criterion: Controls sharpen Aim 1 but do not delay core sampling.

title: Broad-climate simple alternative
core_question: Does broad current climate distance explain capitulum disparity?
prediction: Current subset does not show positive coupling, so new ecology should target microclimate and biotic axes.
required_data: Microclimate and interaction data only if collected with functional design
